The graph of the linear function $y = f(x) + 12$ is shown. If $p$ and $q$ are positive constants, which equation could define $f$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. The graph of $y = f(x) + 12$ can be translated down $12$ units to obtain the graph of $y = f(x)$, so each y-coordinate decreases by $12$. The y-intercept of the graph of $y = f(x) + 12$ is $(0, 5)$, so the y-intercept of $y = f(x)$ is $(0, 5 - 12)$, or $(0, -7)$, which is negative. The shown graph slants downward from left to right, so its slope is negative, and translating the graph does not change its slope; therefore the slope of $y = f(x)$ is also negative. Writing $f(x) = b + mx$ where $b$ is the y-coordinate of the y-intercept and $m$ is the slope, both $b$ and $m$ are negative. Since $p$ and $q$ are positive constants, $f(x) = -q - px$ could define $f$.
